stimulus.body: A 2017 study of 3000 working mothers at gatherings in the American South found 58% acted in line with the crowd, while 12% acted independently.

questions.stem: Which conclusion about crowd behavior in South does the 2017 data support?

options.text: The 2017 South data support collective behavior as the explanation for the crowd behavior pattern.
The 2017 South data support emergent norm as the explanation for the crowd behavior pattern.
options.misconception: assumes crowds have no standards at all

options.text: The 2017 South data support panic as the explanation for the crowd behavior pattern.
options.misconception: labels any fast collective movement as irrational panic

options.text: The 2017 South data support social movement as the explanation for the crowd behavior pattern.
options.misconception: confuses a temporary crowd with a lasting movement

questions.explanation: Relatively spontaneous action by a crowd or mass. The 2017 data from the American South (58% versus 12%) fit this reading; the alternatives describe different mechanisms.
questions.hint: Consider which idea links the finding to wider society.
